subject: feat: generate identicon avatars for users and organizations (#39)
message:
## feat: generate default avatars from account ids

Every user and organization now has a face without anyone uploading one and
without storing a byte: a 5x5 mirrored grid and a hue, both a pure function of
the account id.

`identicon()` lives in packages/shared as a frozen contract rather than in the
web app, since its output decides what every existing account looks like and a
change cannot be migrated or rolled back. Golden vectors pin four seeds; a
plain determinism test would pass for any refactor that silently changed every
face.

Organizations gain an avatar for the first time — the list showed one lucide
glyph for all of them, and member rows showed none despite the API already
sending `image`. The personal row wears the viewer's own face, not one from
the organization's id, so it matches the rail rather than reading as a second
account. Member rows seed from `userId`, not the `member` row id, so one
person looks the same in every organization.

Measured rather than assumed:

- hsl(hue 65% 45%) does not hold contrast. Lightness and chroma are now oklch
  CSS tokens per theme, at the largest chroma in sRGB at every hue: 4.2-4.6:1
  against `muted` in light, 6.3-7.1:1 in dark.
- An unpadded viewBox leaves 14% of a corner cell inside the circular crop,
  hence `-1 -1 7 7`.
- Radix shows the fallback while an image loads, not only on failure, so a
  grid flashed ahead of every photo; `delayMs` suppresses it. The test for
  this needs a genuinely pending image — against one that has already settled
  it passes with or without the delay.

`initials()` is deleted. One `<path>` rather than 25 `<rect>`s, which avoids
seams between cells at 3.43 device pixels and keeps member lists to one node
per avatar.

`organization.logo` stays unexposed: the Better Auth plugin accepts any string
there and our hooks pass it through, so rendering it would let any signed-in
user aim another account's browser — invitations included — at a URL they
chose, with no CSP to stop it. docs/architecture.md records that.

subject: feat(bounties): edit a bounty's scope, hold steps for approval, and pin repository builds as context (#95)
message:
## feat(bounties): hold each step until the steps before it are approved

A step can now be changed only once every step before it is approved.
The price waits on the scope, and the sandbox waits on both. The new
`stepHeldBy` and `stepHeldReason` in core decide this, so the API and
the page refuse with the same words. Going back is never held:
unapproving, removing and unpublishing still work.

- API: pricing (start a run, approve, resize, rubric, respec, reprice)
  and sandbox routes (create, link source, generate, add, change,
  publish, rebuild versions) answer 409 `step_held` with `heldBy` while
  an earlier step is not approved.
- Web: a held step's tab shows a lock and gives the reason in its
  tooltip, and its page opens with a "Locked." banner that links to the
  step holding it. Its actions (Price it, Re-analyze, resize, approve,
  rubric, analyze spec, Create sandbox, Link repo, Publish) are disabled
  and give the reason on hover. The sandbox's generation and publish
  menu use the same reason in place of the old proposal-status checks.

subject: feat(onboarding): connecting Jira sizes nothing; home shows the free category scan (#84)
message:
## feat(web): home adapts to what a workspace has connected

Home is one page that changes with the workspace, decided in
`features/onboarding/setup.ts` from facts `useWorkspaceSetup` reads
through the cache keys the pages it summarises already use:

- Nothing connected: three ways in (Jira, GitHub, write a bounty) over a
  showcase of the six categories, each with what it looks for.
- Jira: the board, opening on its backlog scan. Tickets are sorted into
  the categories for free, and the one in focus is shown as the bounty it
  would become, with one button to size it. Sizing the whole board is
  offered with its cost said first.
- GitHub: the repository's x-ray, with the modules a first bounty is
  easiest to cut from; writing one there opens the new-bounty page on that
  repository and module (`?repo=&area=`, checked against the workspace's
  own list).

A getting-started checklist sits above every stage until it is done or
hidden. The scan is also the board page's first view until the board has
proposals, then folds to one line above them. Nothing on home makes a
model call by itself.

`useConnections` is gone; `useJira` reports a server without Jira as not
offered rather than as a failure.

feat(bounties): select tickets by category and browse proposals by category (#64)
message:
## feat(bounties): size every ticket that fits a category, with the reason

A backlog run took the ten oldest tickets. It now reads the whole board and
sizes every open ticket that fits at least one outsourcing category, and
records why each was picked.

Categories are one registry in packages/core/src/selection: Left behind,
Always next sprint, Quietly wanted, Holding others up, Paper cuts and
Deadline exposed. Each is an id, a label, default thresholds and a rule
built from named signals, so a criterion or a category changes in one
place. The board settings schema is generated from the registry, and a
board can override any threshold or switch a category off.

- Selection reads /board/{id}/issue for every board type, asking for
  sprint history, votes, watchers, links and fix versions, and classifies
  in code. The backlog endpoint hides tickets in a sprint, which are what
  "Always next sprint" looks for. Still no description in a list read.
- The reason is stored on the run's plan and shown on proposal rows, in
  the sizing list, and in the peek under "Why this ticket".
- maxTickets and excludeAssigned become ticketCap (optional, no default)
  and unassignedOnly (default false). Renamed rather than re-defaulted:
  registration stored the old defaults on existing boards, which would
  have kept them capped at ten.
- A run's deadline grows with its plan, and recorded outcomes are bounded
  by the plan rather than a fixed 50.
- Board settings merge category by category and threshold by threshold,
  and a null in an update removes the setting instead of being stored.
- The proposal list pages 50 at a time with "Show more", and title
  streams are split into batches the route accepts.

subject: feat(bounties): sync Jira and repository context into bounties, versioned per source (#80)
message:
## feat(bounties): sync Jira and repository context into bounties, versioned per source

A person can sync a bounty's sources into it as context: its Jira
issue's fields beyond its text (type, status, priority, labels,
components, releases, story points, estimates, demand and links), and
its repository's own documents (README, guides and docs, never code),
read at the newest snapshot and cut to fixed caps
(`packages/core/src/sources.ts`).

Each sync that finds something new is the source's next version in
`bounty_context`; one that finds the same content only moves the
version's revision and check time. The overview holds the latest
version from each source still linked. Sizing and spec drafting are
shown it (`draft-v5`, `jira-size-v4`) and the proposal records the
versions it used; a sandbox version freezes it into its approved task,
which the starter agent is shown (`sandbox_starter@3`), and records the
versions beside it.

- `GET .../bounties/:id/context` says where each source stands:
  unlinked, unsynced, current, ahead of its sync, or unavailable.
- `POST .../bounties/:id/context/{jira,github}/sync` reads the source
  now; a Jira sync takes the issue's text too.

The web bounty page shows each source's sync under its link, warns when
a source has moved past it, and marks the bounty and sandbox steps made
with older context than the overview holds.

Migration 0056 adds `bounty_context` and the context version columns on
`bounty_proposal` and `sandbox_version_source`.
